title: Frère Jacques
subtitle: Chant & piano · premiers pas
credits: Traditional melody and words; new piano arrangement and encoding by Chansonade, CC0 1.0. Traditional French canon, melody and first verse; public-domain declaration and French text in the source score. Sung once in unison, without overlapping canon entries.

title: Au clair de la lune
subtitle: Chant & piano · premiers pas
credits: Traditional melody and words; new piano arrangement and encoding by Chansonade, CC0 1.0. Traditional melody and first verse, historical witness: J.-B. Weckerlin, Chansons et rondes enfantines, Garnier, 1870, pp. 32–33. No historical piano accompaniment or modern editorial prose is copied.

title: Une souris verte
subtitle: Chant & piano · premiers pas

title: Are You Sleeping? (Brother John)
subtitle: Chant & piano · premiers pas
credits: Traditional melody and words; new piano arrangement and encoding by Chansonade, CC0 1.0. Traditional English first verse on the Frère Jacques tune; English lyrics are printed in the source PDF, declared public domain. Unison learning version, no overlapping canon entries.

title: Twinkle, Twinkle, Little Star
subtitle: Chant & piano · premiers pas
credits: Traditional melody and words; new piano arrangement and encoding by Chansonade, CC0 1.0. Traditional Ah! vous dirai-je, maman melody; first stanza of The Star by Jane Taylor (1806), with the customary closing repetition. Historical notation witness: The Child’s Own Music Book, 1918. Piano newly composed; historical piano arrangement not copied.

title: Row, Row, Row Your Boat
subtitle: Chant & piano · premiers pas
credits: Traditional melody and words; new piano arrangement and encoding by Chansonade, CC0 1.0. Melody and standard verse credited to E. O. Lyte in 55 Songs and Choruses for Community Singing, 1917; source scan declares public domain. Melody only transcribed, in a unison learning version; piano is new.

title: Bruder Jakob
subtitle: Chant & piano · premiers pas
credits: Traditional melody and words; new piano arrangement and encoding by Chansonade, CC0 1.0. Traditional German verse and Frère Jacques melody, source declares anonymous public-domain material. Unison learning version, no overlapping canon entries.

title: Alle meine Entchen
subtitle: Chant & piano · premiers pas
credits: Traditional melody and words; new piano arrangement and encoding by Chansonade, CC0 1.0. Traditional first stanza and melody variant from the source LilyPond score, transposed from D to C major; quarter-note phrase endings followed by rests preserved. Source declares public domain. Its chord symbols and other verses are not reused.

title: Hänschen klein
subtitle: Chant & piano · premiers pas
credits: Traditional melody and words; new piano arrangement and encoding by Chansonade, CC0 1.0. Traditional tune and short one-stanza text exactly as the source’s public-domain C-major melody edition; its piano/chord arrangement is not copied. The older multi-stanza text by Franz Wiedemann is not substituted.

title: Vader Jacob
subtitle: Chant & piano · premiers pas
credits: Traditional melody and words; new piano arrangement and encoding by Chansonade, CC0 1.0. Traditional Dutch verse explicitly marked Publiek domein by Wikisource; traditional Frère Jacques melody. Unison version. The page gives no scanned publication witness; this provenance limitation is recorded in PUBLIC_CATALOG.md.

title: Altijd is Kortjakje ziek
subtitle: Chant & piano · premiers pas
credits: Traditional melody and words; new piano arrangement and encoding by Chansonade, CC0 1.0. Traditional Dutch verse from Simon Abramsz., Rijmpjes en versjes uit de oude doos, p. 65 (collection first published 1910; DBNL witness is a later printing). Historical words “boek met zilverwerk” preserved; closing repetition added on the traditional Ah! vous dirai-je, maman melody. No illustrations, page layout or modern piano arrangement reused.

title: Ik zag twee beren
subtitle: Chant & piano · premiers pas
credits: Traditional melody and words; new piano arrangement and encoding by Chansonade, CC0 1.0. Melody and one verse manually transcribed from Florimond van Duyse, Het oude Nederlandsche lied, vol. 2, 1905, pp. 1833–1834, variant V citing G. J. Boekenoogen’s 1896 collection. Historical words “’k Zag” and final “na” retained. No modern commercial arrangement reused.
